Watch Dog Timer

This sample demonstrates using a GPIO interrupt to trigger a watchdog feed operation, restarting the watchdog timer WDT.

When the GPIO detects a falling edge input, it triggers a GPIO interrupt, and within the interrupt function, the watchdog feed operation is performed, restarting the watchdog timer.

If the watchdog feed operation is not performed within the WDT's set time, the WDT will execute a reset operation.

Users can change the WDT configuration, GPIO pin configuration, and other information in the sample through different macro configurations. For specific macro configurations, see Configurations.

Requirements

For requirements, please refer to the Requirements.

Wiring

Connect P4_0 to external input signal.

Configurations

  1. The following macros can be configured to choose between using CORE WDT or AON WDT.

    #define USE_WDT                 1
#define USE_AON_WDT             0
#define USE_WDT_SELECT          USE_WDT       /*< Set this macro to select CORE WDT or AON WDT. */

  2. The following macros can be configured to modify the pin definitions.

    #define INPUT_PIN           P4_0              /*< Set this macro to modify GPIO Pin. */
#define GPIO_PIN_IRQN       GPIOB5_IRQn
#define GPIO_Pin_Handler    GPIOB5_Handler

Building and Downloading

For building and downloading, please refer to the Building and Downloading.

Experimental Verification

  1. After resetting the EVB, observe the log information as shown in the Debug Analyzer.

    Start wdt test!

  2. The watchdog timer interval is set to 10 seconds. If the external input signal changes from a high level to a low level within 10 seconds, it triggers a GPIO interrupt and performs a watchdog feed operation, printing a log.

    [APP]  !**[app] app_handle_io_msg: feeding dog, restart wdg timer.

  3. If no dog feeding operation is performed within 10 seconds, the EVB will restart automatically.

Code Overview

This section introduces the code and process description for initialization and corresponding function implementation in the sample.

Source Code Directory

The directory for project file and source code are as follows:

  • Project directory: sdk\samples\peripheral\wdt\wdt\proj

  • Source code directory: sdk\samples\peripheral\wdt\wdt\src

Initialization

The initialization flow for peripherals can refer to Initialization Flow in General Introduction.

  1. In the main function, call os_sched_start to start task scheduling. In app_main_task, create a message queue and call driver_init to initialize the GPIO and WDT peripherals.

    void app_main_task(void *p_param)
{
    ...
    os_msg_queue_create(&io_queue_handle, "io queue", MAX_NUMBER_OF_IO_MESSAGE,  sizeof(uint32_t));
    os_msg_queue_create(&evt_queue_handle, "evt queue", MAX_NUMBER_OF_EVENT_MESSAGE, sizeof(uint32_t));

    driver_init();
    while (true)
    ...
}

void driver_init(void)
{
    driver_gpio_init();
    driver_wdt_init();
}

  2. For detailed initialization of the GPIO peripheral, refer to GPIO Initialization in GPIO Input Interrupt

  3. Initialize the WDT peripheral:

    1. If the configuration macro USE_WDT_SELECT is set to USE_WDT, call the WDT_Start() function to enable the WDT feature, set the timer to 10 seconds, and trigger EVB RESET_ALL if not fed on time.

    2. If the configuration macro USE_WDT_SELECT is set to USE_AON_WDT, call the AON_WDT_Start() function to enable the AON WDT feature, set the timer to 10 seconds, and trigger EVB RESET_ALL if not fed on time.

    void driver_wdt_init(void)
{
    /* WDT timing 10s. */
#if USE_WDT_SELECT
    WDT_Start(10000, RESET_ALL);
#else
    AON_WDT_Start(AON_WDT, 10000, RESET_ALL);
#endif
}

Functional Implementation

  1. After enabling the WDT function, the system will start a 10-second timer.

  2. Within the timing period, when P4_0 detects an external falling edge signal input, it will trigger a GPIO interrupt. In the interrupt handler, a message of type IO_MSG_TYPE_GPIO will be sent. In the message handler, WDT_Kick() or AON_WDT_Kick() is called to perform a watchdog kick operation to reset the watchdog timer.

    void GPIO_Pin_Handler(void)
{
    /* Mask and disable interrupt */
    ...

    uint32_t send_val = IO_MSG_TYPE_GPIO;
    if (false == app_send_msg_to_apptask(&send_val))
    {
        APP_PRINT_ERROR0("[io_gpio] GPIO_Input_Handler: Send int_gpio_msg failed!");
        //Add user code here!
        GPIO_ClearINTPendingBit(GPIO_PORT, GPIO_PIN);
        return;
    }

    /* Clear int flag, unmask and enable interrupt */
    ...
}

void app_handle_io_msg(uint32_t io_msg)
{
    switch (io_msg)
    {

    case IO_MSG_TYPE_GPIO:
        {
            APP_PRINT_INFO0("[app] app_handle_io_msg: feeding dog, restart wdg timer.");
            wdt_feed();
        }
        break;
    default:
        break;
    }
}

void wdt_feed(void)
{
#if USE_WDT_SELECT
    WDT_Kick();
#else
    AON_WDT_Kick(AON_WDT);
#endif
}

  3. If P4_0 does not detect an external falling edge signal input within the timing period, meaning no watchdog kick operation is performed, the system will perform a reset operation.
